{{Short description|Taiwanese plant pathologist}}
{{Orphan|date=December 2023}}

'''Yu Su-may''' ({{zh|t=余淑美}}; born 3 November 1952) is a Taiwanese plant pathologist.

Yu was born on 3 November 1952,<ref name="twas"/> and graduated from [[National Chung Hsing University]] with bachelor's and master's degrees in plant pathology.<ref name="imbas">{{cite news |title=Dr. Su-May Yu 余淑美 博士 Distinguished Research Fellow, IMB |url=https://www.imb.sinica.edu.tw/~sumay/ |access-date=12 December 2023 |publisher=Institute of Molecular Biology, Academia Sinica}}</ref> She then moved to the United States to attend the [[University of Arkansas]] between 1980 and 1984, where she completed a doctorate in plant biology and pathology.<ref name="imbas"/><ref name="as"/> Yu pursued postdoctoral research at [[Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory]], the [[University of Rochester]], and [[Cornell University]] before returning to Taiwan for an associate research fellow position at the Academia Sinica's Institute of Molecular Biology in 1989.<ref name="imbas"/><ref name="as"/> She was successively named a research fellow in 1997 and a distinguished research fellow in 2008.<ref name="imbas"/><ref name="as"/>

Yu was elected a fellow of [[The World Academy of Sciences]] in 2005,<ref name="twas">{{cite news |title=YU Su-May |url=https://twas.org/directory/yu-su-may |access-date=12 December 2023 |publisher=The World Academy of Sciences}}</ref> a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in 2009,<ref name="aaas2009">{{cite news |title=AAAS Fellows |url=https://www.aaas.org/sites/default/files/AnnualReports/2009/aaas_ann_rpt_09l_fellows.pdf |access-date=12 December 2023 |publisher=American Association for the Advancement of Science}}</ref> and a member of [[Academia Sinica]] in 2012.<ref name="as">{{cite news |title=Su-May Yu |url=https://academicians.sinica.edu.tw/index.php?r=academician-n%2Fshow&id=646 |access-date=12 December 2023 |publisher=Academia Sinica}}</ref>

In 2014, Yu won the Outstanding Award of the [[Taiwan Outstanding Women in Science Awards]] for her research on plant [[molecular biology]] and [[locus control region]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.taiwan-panorama.com/en/Articles/Details?Guid=f0f976ee-c880-44f6-9e72-f92be5c0b04b&CatId=10&postname=Remaking%20Our%20World%E2%80%94Outstanding%20Taiwanese%20Women%20in%20Science |title=Remaking Our World—Outstanding Taiwanese Women in Science |author=Chang Chiung-fang |publisher=[[Taiwan Panorama]] |access-date=2026-04-10 |date=August 2014 |language=en}}</ref>
